recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-25206 unless a later work-group decision chooses to remove or rewrite remaining example/profile uses of the deprecated but still valid pattern discriminator.
issue_request: FHIR-25206 was a Published/Persuasive R5 FHIR-core change request asking to merge the value and pattern slicing discriminator types, deprecate one because both were already normative, allow valueset binding, fixed[x], and pattern[x] declarations under the same discriminator semantics, make pattern work like value, and add a good-practice warning that pattern[x] is generally preferable to fixed[x].
initial_application: No historical commit tagged FHIR-25206 was found in the relevant profiling or ElementDefinition source history. The requested behavior is present through adjacent and later changes: profiling.html describes value slicing as using fixed values, pattern values, or required value set bindings and states pattern is equivalent for backward compatibility; datatypes/elementdefinition.xml records pattern as deprecated/equivalent and includes the fixed[x] best-practice warning.
additional_context: The linked Zulip discussions show the original ambiguity and use case for mixing pattern and value set binding; FHIR-I minutes on 2020-03-02 confirm the formal decision to deprecate pattern and document that value allows slicing by pattern. Later FHIR-34152 work, already present on the combined branch, expanded fixed[x] versus pattern[x] explanation and links without changing the FHIR-25206 decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current build-scoped FHIR core source already conveys the approved semantics and warning. No source edit was necessary.

related_jiras.note: Added the current fixed[x] versus pattern[x] explanation and links; already represented on the combined branch and not decided again.
Clarified the required binding parenthetical in the same profiling discriminator list but did not change the merge/deprecation decision.
